$meta.name: Radius design tokens
$meta.note: Primitives below are the exact values bound as Figma variables. The `semantic` block is NOT transcribed from Figma -- only primitives are bound as variables there. The semantic layer is designed here, by role, per the brief in mobile/design-tokens/README.md. Reference syntax `{color.ink.950}` means "resolve this value from the path given"; see scripts/generate.mjs for the resolver.
$meta.contrastMethod: WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula, sRGB. See scripts/generate.mjs verifyContrast(). All ratios in README.md#accessibility were computed by that code, not eyeballed.

familyLicense.note: Both OFL (open licence). Fraunces: Undercase Type, distributed via Google Fonts / GitHub (github.com/undercasetype/Fraunces). Inter: Rasmus Andersson, distributed via Google Fonts / GitHub (github.com/rsms/inter). Font FILES are not included here -- only the family-name tokens. Bundling .ttf/.otf resources or wiring Android Downloadable Fonts is a delivery-mechanism decision for android-kotlin/ios-swift and is out of scope for this handoff; do not add a font dependency without asking (ORCHESTRATION §8: new 3rd-party dependency of any kind requires escalation).

letterSpacingUnit.confidence: assumed, not confirmed by Figma API unit field -- see README.md#overline-tracking for the reasoning and the open question filed against the overline row below.

overline.flag: 5x jump from label.s (1.5) with no intermediate step. Almost certainly intentional editorial-style eyebrow tracking (uppercase micro-labels conventionally run much wider than the rest of a type ramp), but confirm with Figma source before treating as load-bearing. See README.md#overline-tracking.

spacing.note: 4pt base grid, exactly as specified. Not all multiples of 4 -- 6 is a deliberate half-step.

elevation.note: Verbatim from Figma Foundations: "On dark, elevation = surface lightening + hairline. Shadow is secondary." No shadow blur/offset/opacity values were given as Figma variables, so none are fabricated here -- levels are expressed as a surface-lightening + hairline ladder only. If/when Figma specifies real shadow specs, add them as a new `elevation.shadow` block; do not guess blur/spread now.

dark.$note: The only fully specified theme. Figma Foundations bound no light-mode primitives (checked -- only the dark-first ramp above exists as variables), so a light theme is NOT fabricated here. See README.md#light-theme for the open item. RadiusTheme.kt forcing dark unconditionally is therefore correct today, not a shortcut.

canvas.role: elev/0. App background, the default canvas behind everything.

sunken.role: Recessed wells: text-input fill, code/mono blocks. Darker than canvas, used sparingly.

base.role: elev/1. Default content surface -- screens, list rows, nav bar container.

raised.role: elev/2. Cards, chips, tiles sitting above base content.

modal.role: elev/4. Sheets, dialogs, full modals -- the top of the stack.

primary.role: Default text/icon colour. Safe on every surface -- see contrast table.

secondary.role: De-emphasised but still-informational text (subtitles, metadata, timestamps). Safe on every surface.

tertiary.restriction: AA (4.5:1) only on surface.canvas (4.69:1) and surface.base (4.52:1). On surface.raised/overlay/modal it drops to 4.29/3.98/3.60 -- large text or icons ONLY on those three surfaces, never small body copy.

disabled.restriction: FAILS WCAG AA and even the 3:1 large-text/UI floor on every surface (2.48-2.71:1 measured). WCAG explicitly exempts inactive/disabled controls from 1.4.3 and 1.4.11, which is the only reason this token is legal. Never use it for anything a user is meant to read as live information, and never let colour be the only disabled cue -- pair with reduced elevation, removed interactivity, or explicit disabled affordance (root CLAUDE.md 'never colour alone').

onFill.role: Text/icon drawn on top of any saturated /400 accent or status fill (ember, signal, bloom, success, warning, danger, info). Verified 5.14-9.96:1 across all seven -- one token, always safe, never guess between light-on-fill and dark-on-fill per accent.

onWash.role: Text/icon drawn on an accent WASH surface (ember/700, signal/600, bloom/600). Verified 5.20-7.02:1 across all three. Do NOT use the accent's own light step as onWash text/icon colour -- see README.md#wash-text, it fails on two of three accents.

hairline.role: Decorative dividers between static content (list separators, section rules) where the surface-colour step already carries the boundary.
hairline.restriction: 1.14-1.18:1 against canvas/base -- fails the 3:1 non-text floor (WCAG 1.4.11). Legal ONLY because a plain content divider is not a UI component under 1.4.11. Never use as the sole edge of a tappable/focusable element.

subtle.role: Default resting border for cards/containers, always paired with a fill or elevation difference.
subtle.restriction: 1.44-1.49:1 -- also fails 3:1. Must never be the ONLY boundary cue of an interactive element (that is what border.interactive is for).

interactive.role: The boundary of any control where the border IS the sole visual edge: text-input outlines, OutlinedButton, segmented controls, non-accent focus rings.
interactive.verified: 4.52-4.69:1 against canvas/base -- clears the 3:1 non-text floor with margin.

danger.verified: 5.14-5.33:1 against canvas/base -- clears 3:1 comfortably, also clears 4.5:1 if reused as error text.

accent.$note: Root CLAUDE.md: 'one accent per screen. two competing golds = one is wrong.' Four accents exist, each SCOPED to a specific mode or moment -- they are never meant to co-occur as two competing primaries on one screen.

discover.$scope: DISCOVER mode (online dating). Root CLAUDE.md: accent=gold ember/400.

pressed.role: Pressed/active state of an ember-filled control.

wash.role: Subtle tinted background for an ember chip/badge on a dark surface. Pair with content.onWash for text, never the accent's own light tone for text (see restriction on content.onWash).

radar.$scope: RADAR mode (BLE proximity). Root CLAUDE.md: accent=teal signal/400. RESERVED -- root CLAUDE.md: 'signal teal is RESERVED for Radar/BLE/offline. using it elsewhere breaks the mental model.' Do not reuse signal/* for anything outside Radar/BLE/offline-state UI.

pressed.role: Pressed/active state of a signal-filled control.

wash.role: Subtle tinted background for a signal chip/badge on a dark surface. Pair with content.onWash for text.

like.$scope: The like/match moment specifically -- Discover's Likes You / Standouts, match celebration, mutual-wave confirmation. Bloom is deliberately its own accent, not a Discover sub-shade of ember: a screen dedicated to a like/match moment may make bloom its ONE primary accent for that screen (still obeys 'one accent per screen' -- it replaces ember for that screen, it does not join it).

pressed.role: Pressed/active state of a bloom-filled control.

wash.role: Subtle tinted background for a like/match chip or badge. Pair with content.onWash for text.

threads.$scope: THREADS: one inbox, both origins, favours neither. Deliberately NOT a hue -- a saturated Threads colour would imply Threads is its own mode competing with Discover/Radar, which contradicts 'one inbox, label transport.'

default.verified: 10.75-11.15:1 against canvas/base -- used for selected-tab / active-indicator states without introducing a fourth hue.

status.$note: Figma Foundations only bound a single /400 stop for success/warning/danger/info (unlike ink/ember/bloom/signal, which have 3-14 stops each). That blocks defining pressed/wash variants without inventing hex. Filed as a finding in README.md#status-ramp-gap -- do not invent shades to fill this in. Status colours here are restricted to `default` (text/icon/small filled dot) and reuse content.onFill for anything drawn on a status fill; there is no status wash tier.

default.verified: 8.09-8.39:1 as text/icon on canvas/base; 8.39:1 for content.onFill on a success-filled dot/badge.
9.09-9.42:1 as text/icon on canvas/base; 9.42:1 for content.onFill on a warning-filled dot/badge.
5.14-5.33:1 as text/icon on canvas/base; 5.33:1 for content.onFill on a danger-filled dot/badge. Same primitive as border.danger -- one value, two roles, by design.
6.55-6.79:1 as text/icon on canvas/base; 6.79:1 for content.onFill on an info-filled dot/badge.

state.$note: No opacity/alpha tokens exist in the primitive set, so states are expressed as token SWAPS (a different named colour, or a different elevation surface), never as a computed alpha overlay. This is deliberate, not a gap: it keeps every visible state expressible as 'which named token', auditable the same way as everything else.

disabled.note: Prefer Material3's own built-in disabled-state alpha for stock M3 components (it already does the right thing for enabled=false). Reserve these tokens for custom-drawn muted/inactive content that is not a disableable M3 component.

focus.note: Focus ring colour is contextual: use the active mode's accent inside a mode screen, fall back to content.primary (neutral, 14-18:1 everywhere) outside a mode context (Settings, onboarding, etc).
